```{r define-functions, include = FALSE}
# Define functions

## Reads in Data from all sheets at once + manipulation to extract only relevant data
read_all <- function(filename, tibble = TRUE) {
    # If tibble is preferred over data.frame use "tibble = TRUE"
    sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(filename)
    x <- lapply(sheets, function(y) readxl::read_excel(filename, sheet = y))
    x <- lapply(x, function(y) as.data.frame(y))
    x <- lapply(x, function(y) y %>% mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.factor)))
    names(x) <- sheets
    x
}

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Function for data transformation
DatTrans <- function(x, depVar, indVar, Drop_Col = NULL, Remove_From = NULL, Term = NULL, Type = NULL) {
    
    # prompts selection of number corresponding to transformation
    aa <- readline("Choose transformation:
    0 = None
    Mod skew (sqrt):
    1 = + ; 2 = -
    Hi skew (nl):
    3 = + ; 4 = -
    Hir skew (log10):
    5 = + ; 6 = -
    Ext skew (Inverse):
    7 = + ; 8 = -
    Other:
    9 = Box-Cox") 
    
    # In case of negative values in the raw data; the data is translated, thus the smallest values becomes 1
    if (any(x[c(depVar)] < 0)) { 
        
      print("Translated to min = 1")
      
      x <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(all_of(depVar), ~ (.x + 1 - min(.x))))
        
    } else {
      
      print("Raw Data")
      
      x <- x
      
    }
    
    
    # Executes the selected transformation
    if (as.numeric(aa) == 1) {
      
      z <- "Square Root Transformed (+)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>%
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ sqrt(.x + 1)))
      
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 2) {
      
      z <- "Square Root Transformed (-)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>%
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ sqrt(max(.x + 1) - .x)))
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 3) {
      
      z <- "Natural Log Transformed (+)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ log(.x + 1)))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 4) {
      
      z <- "Natural Log Transformed (-)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ log(max(.x + 1) - .x)))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 5) {
      
      z <- "Log10 Transformed (+)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ log10(.x + 1)))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 6) {
      
      z <- "Log10 Transformed (-)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ log10(max(.x + 1) - .x)))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 7) {
      
      z <- "Inverse Transformed (+)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ (1 / (.x + 1))))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 8) {
      
      z <- "Inverse Transformed (-)"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x %>% 
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ (1 / (max(.x + 1) - .x))))
        
      
    } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 9) {
      
      z <- "Box-Cox power Transformed"
      print(z)
      
      if (is.null(Drop_Col)) { # In case some rows need to be removed
        
        y <- x %>%
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ (.x + 1)))
        
      } else if (Drop_Col == "Yes") {
        
        y <- x %>% # Splitting "Measure" variable back into two columns according to "Measure_Type"
        .[!.[,Remove_From] %in% Term,] %>%
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ (.x + 1)))
        
      } else {
        
        print("error")
        
        stop("Please, define `Drop_Col` with NULL or `Yes`")
      }
      
      indVar <- indVar[indVar %in% names(y)] # In case, column names do not exist, these are dropped
      
      Mod <- lm(formula = as.formula(paste0("cbind(", paste(depVar, collapse = ", "), ") ~ ", paste(indVar, collapse = " * "))), data = y) # Run the linear model
      
      bc <- powerTransform(Mod)$lambda %>%
        setNames(depVar) # Do the Box-Cox power Transformation
    
      y <- x %>%
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ (.x + 1))) %>% # Modify outcome variables with respective lambda term
        mutate(across(any_of(depVar), ~ bcPower(.x, bc[cur_column()])))  
      
      
      } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 0) {
      
      z <- "untransformed"
      print(z)
      
      y <- x
      
      } else {
      
        print("Wrong input")
        stop()
      }
    
    output <- list("Data" = y, "Transformation" = z)
    
    output
}

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Adjusts for Skewness and Kurtosis, if needed
ModSkeKur <- function(x, depVar, indVar, Type = "h") {
  
  # prompts selection of number corresponding to transformation
    aa <- readline("Choose transformation:
                   0 = None
                   1 = MLE_LambertW")
      
  x <- x %>% 
        mutate(., x %>%
                 dplyr::select(any_of(indVar)) %>%
                 as.data.frame(.) %>%
                 mutate(., across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>% 
                 unite(., "IDs", sep = "_", remove = TRUE) %>% 
                 mutate(., across("IDs", as.factor)))
  
  if (as.numeric(aa) == 1) {
    
    w <- "Lambert W transformed"
    print(w)
    
    # Correct for kurtosis by Lambert W      
    z <- sapply(depVar, function(a) {
      
      sapply(levels(x$IDs), function(y) {
    
        mod.Lh <- get_input(
          MLE_LambertW(x[x$IDs %in% y, a], 
                               distname = "normal", 
                               type = Type)
          ) %>%
          enframe(.) %>%
          .[,2] 
        
      }, simplify = FALSE) %>%
        bind_rows(.) %>%
        as.data.frame(.)
      
    }, simplify = FALSE) %>%
      bind_cols(.) %>%
      as.data.frame(.) %>%
      set_colnames(depVar)
    
    # Replace with adjusted data
    y <- x %>% 
      arrange(IDs) %>%
      sjmisc::replace_columns(., z) %>%
      .[, !names(.) %in% "IDs"]
    
  } else if (as.numeric(aa) == 0) {
    
    w <- "untransformed"
    print(w)
    
    y <- x %>%
      .[, !names(.) %in% "IDs"]
    
  } else {
      
    print("Wrong input for cc")
    stop()
  }
  
  output <- list("Data" = y, "Transformation" = w)
    
  output
}
```

```{r adjustable-variable-information, include = FALSE}
#
## Raw data folder
RawDat <- "Data"

RawDatSub <- "WBC counts"

ColNamBld <- c("Pre-Treatment", "Pre-Infestation", "Post-Infestation")

BldTyp <- c("WBC", "LYMPH", "NEUT", "MONO", "EO", "BASO")
```

```{r two-way-Mixed-ANOVA-FTY720-blood-samples, include = FALSE}
# LOADING DATA #################################################################

## Get data directory
survival_dir <- file.path(here::here(), RawDat, RawDatSub)
## List all excel files in directory as full directory names
survival_files <- list.files(survival_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)

## Stop the script if no files are found
stopifnot(length(survival_files) >= 1)

## Load all data from all files contained within the directory
DatBld <- purrr::map(survival_files, read_all) %>%
  purrr::set_names(str_extract(survival_files, "(?<=counts/).*(?= Blood)"))

## Get the metadata from "DatBld" for each tick species
MetDatBld <- lapply(DatBld, function(zz) {
  
  zz[["Groups"]]
})

## Remove the "Groups" dataframe
DatBld <- lapply(DatBld, function(zz) {
  
  zz[! names(zz) %in% "Groups"]
})

# Normalize data by respective RBC counts; normalized to 5 [10^6 / ul]
DatBld <- lapply(DatBld, function(zz) {
  lapply(zz, function(yy) {
    replace(yy, colnames(yy) %in% ColNamBld, t(t(yy[, ColNamBld]) * unlist(5 / yy[yy$Type == "RBC", ColNamBld])))
  })
})

# Split dataframes into respective treatment groups
DatBld <- mapply(function(xx, yy) {
  lapply(levels(xx$Group), function(zz) {
  yy[as.character(xx[xx$Group == zz,]$Guinea_Pig %>% droplevels())] }) %>%
  setNames(levels(xx$Group))
}, xx = MetDatBld,
   yy = DatBld,
   SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# Merge data into one dataframe
DatBld <- lapply(DatBld, function(xx) {
  xx %>%
    purrr::map(., ~ bind_rows(.x, .id = "Guinea_Pig")) %>%
    bind_rows(., .id = "State") %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = ColNamBld,
                 names_to = "Treatment",
                 values_to = "Counts") %>%
    dplyr::filter(if_all("Type", ~ .x %in% BldTyp)) %>%
    droplevels(.) %>%
    as.data.frame(.) %>%
    mutate(., across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
    split(., f = .$Type)
})
```

```{r WBC-data-analysis-by-two-way-mixed-anova, include = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
# Data analysis
ResBld <- lapply(DatBld, function(aa) {
  
  lapply(list(aa[["LYMPH"]]), function(bb) {
  
  # Extract the data by experiment
  BldCnt <- bb %>%
              dplyr::select(any_of(c("Guinea_Pig", "State", "Treatment", "Counts"))) %>%
              mutate(., across(where(is.integer), as.numeric)) %>%
              droplevels(.) %>%
              mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
  
  BldCnt$Treatment <- forcats::fct_rev(BldCnt$Treatment)
    
    # Generate raw data backup
    BldCnt2 <- BldCnt
    
  
  # DATA VISUALIZATION by box plot
  DatDis <- ggplot(BldCnt , 
                   aes(x = State, y = Counts, fill = Treatment)) + 
    geom_boxplot()

  
  # SUMMARY STATISTICS
  SumStat <- BldCnt %>%
    group_by(State, Treatment) %>%
    get_summary_stats(Counts, type = "full")
  
  
# ASSUMPTION TESTING ###########################################################

  # 1. NORMALITY ---------------------------------------------------------------
  
  # Data normality check and transformation loop
  for (aa in 1:100) {
    
    # 1.1 Normality of groups (pre-transformation decision)
    NormUV <- BldCnt %>% 
      group_by(State, Treatment) %>%
      rstatix::shapiro_test(Counts) %>%
      mutate("Outcome" = ifelse(.$p <= 0.05, "sig.", "ns"))
      
      print(NormUV)
      
    # Skewness and kurtosis check by group (pre-transformation decision)
    SkeKur <- lapply(list(BldCnt), function(x) {
      
      Skew <- x %>%
        group_by(State, Treatment) %>%
        metan::skew(.)
      
        if (any(Skew$Counts > 1)) {
  
          SkewOut <- "Right skew"
          
        } else if (any(Skew$Counts < -1)) {
  
          SkewOut <- "Left skew"
          
        } else {
  
          SkewOut <- "No skew"
        }
      
      Kurt <- x %>%
        group_by(State, Treatment) %>%
        metan::kurt(.)
        
        if (any(Kurt$Counts > 2)) {
  
          KurtOut <- "Leptokurtic"
          
        } else if (any(Kurt$Counts < -2)) {
  
          KurtOut <- "Platykurtic"
          
        } else {
  
          KurtOut <- "Mesokurtic"
        }
      
      list("Skewness: Result" = SkewOut,
           "Skewness: Data"   = Skew, 
           "Kurtosis: Result" = KurtOut,
           "Kurtosis: Data"   = Kurt)
      
    }) %>%
      purrr::flatten(.)
    
      print(SkeKur)
    
    # Make decision about data transformation   
    bb <- readline("Continue loop?
                   0 = Leave loop
                   1 = Standard Transformation
                   2 = LambertW Transformation
                   3 = Revert to raw data")
    
    # Data transformation loop
    if (bb == 0) { # leave the loop
      
      break
      
    } else if (bb == 1) { # Transform the data
      
      # DATA TRANSFORMATION 
      BldCnt <- DatTrans(BldCnt,
                         # Name all dependent variables
                         depVar = "Counts",
                         # Name all independent variables (predictors)
                         indVar = c("State", "Treatment"))
      
      # Separate transformation information into separate variable
      ResTrans <- BldCnt[["Transformation"]]
      
        print(ResTrans)
        
      # Convert transformed data back into a dataframe
      BldCnt <- BldCnt[!names(BldCnt) %in% "Transformation"] %>%
        purrr::flatten(.) %>%
        bind_cols(.) %>%
        as.data.frame(.)
      
    } else if (bb == 2) {
      
      # Choose to apply Lambert W or not
      BldCnt <- ModSkeKur(BldCnt,
                          # Name all dependent variables
                          depVar = "Counts",
                          # Name all independent variables (predictors)
                          indVar = c("State", "Treatment"), 
                          Type = "h")
      
      # Separate transformation information into separate variable
      ResTransSK <- BldCnt[["Transformation"]]
    
        print(ResTransSK)
      
      # Convert transformed data back into a dataframe
      BldCnt <- BldCnt[!names(BldCnt) %in% "Transformation"] %>%
        purrr::flatten(.) %>%
        as.data.frame(.)
      
    } else if (bb == 3) {
      
      # Revert to raw data in case transformation did not work out
      BldCnt <- BldCnt2
    }
  }
  
  # In case no transformation was executed  
  if (exists("ResTrans") == FALSE & exists("ResTransSK") == FALSE) {
    
    ResTrans <- "untransformed"
    print(ResTrans)
    
    ResTransSK <- "untransformed"
    print(ResTransSK)
    
  } else if (exists("ResTrans") == FALSE) {
    
    ResTrans <- "untransformed"
    print(ResTrans)
    
  } else if (exists("ResTransSK") == FALSE) {
    
    ResTransSK <- "untransformed"
    print(ResTransSK)
  }
  
    # Data visualization: QQ-plot
    qqplotBld <- ggpubr::ggqqplot(BldCnt, "Counts", ggtheme = theme_bw()) +
    facet_grid(Treatment ~ State, labeller = "label_both")
      
    
  # 1.2 Multivariate normality
  # Build the linear model
  Mod  <- lm(Counts ~ Treatment * State,
               data = BldCnt)
    
    # Compute Shapiro-Wilk test of normality
    NormRes <- shapiro_test(residuals(Mod))

    # Create a QQ plot of residuals
    qqplotRes <- ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(Mod), ggtheme = theme_bw())
    
  
    # 2. OUTLIERS---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Calculation of outliers
    OutLierUV <- BldCnt %>% # Untransformed data
      group_by(., across(any_of(c("Treatment", "State")))) %>%
      identify_outliers(Counts) %>%
      .[, c(1:3, (ncol(.)-1):ncol(.))]
    
      # Box-plot for visual assessment of outliers
      BoxPlotUV <- ggboxplot(BldCnt,
                             x = "State", 
                             y = "Counts",
                             color = "Treatment",
                             palette = "jco"
                             )
      
    
    # 3. HOMOGENEITY OF VARIANCES-----------------------------------------------
    
    # Testing for homogeneity of variance between the groups of the between-subjects factors for each level of the within-subjects factors
    EquVar <- BldCnt %>% # If violated, transformation may resolve the issue, or a robust mixed ANOVA can be applied
      group_by(Treatment) %>%
      levene_test(Counts ~ State, data = .)
    
      # Residual vs Fitted plot to assess variance by group
      plot.new()
      plot(Mod, 1)
      EquVarPlot <- recordPlot()
    
  
      # 4. HOMOGENEITY OF COVARIANCES---------------------------------------------
    
    BoxM <- box_m(BldCnt[, "Counts", drop = FALSE], BldCnt$State) # Test homogeneity of covariance in the between-subject factor; the test is highly sensitive, thus, consider p<0.001 as significance threshold
    
    
    # 5. SPHERICITY-------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mauchly's test executed automatically within anova_test() function, if within-subjects factor has >2 levels. For two within-subjects factor levels, the sphericity assumption hold by default. Here, we only have two levels in the within-subjects factor: "Ticks_Placed"
      
    # Two-way Mixed ANOVA (standard) for Maulchy's test
      Spher <- rstatix::anova_test( # This version is suitable if there are no ouliers
          data = BldCnt, dv = Counts, wid = Guinea_Pig,
          between = State, within = Treatment
          ) # Greenhouse-Geisser sphericity correction automatically applied if Mauchly's test is significant (p<0.05)
      
      
  # RESULTS OF ASSUMPTION TESTING-------------------------------------------------
    if (any(NormUV$p <= 0.05)) {
      ResNormUV <- "Univariate: Non-Guassian"
      print(ResNormUV)
    } else {
      ResNormUV <- "Univariate: Guassian"
      print(ResNormUV)
    }
    
    if (NormRes$p.value <= 0.05) {
      ResNormRes <- "Residuals: Non-Guassian"
      print(ResNormRes)
    } else {
      ResNormRes <- "Residuals: Guassian"
      print(ResNormRes)
    }
    if (dim(OutLierUV)[1] != 0) {
      ResOutUV <- paste0(dim(OutLierUV)[1], " ", 
                      paste(gsub( ".*\\.", "", names(OutLierUV %>% 
                                                       dplyr::select(where(~any(.x == TRUE)))))[c(2,1)] %>% 
                              .[!is.na(.)], collapse = " "),
                      "(s) found")
      print(ResOutUV)
    } else {
      ResOutUV <- "No outliers"
      print(ResOutUV)
    }
    
    if (any(EquVar$p <= 0.05)) {
      ResEquVar <- "Heterogenous variance"
      print(ResEquVar)
    } else {
      ResEquVar <- "Homogeneous variance"
      print(ResEquVar)
    }
    
    if (BoxM$p.value <= 0.001) {
      ResEquCoV <- "Heterogenous covariance"
      print(ResEquCoV)
    } else {
      ResEquCoV <- "Homogeneous covariance"
      print(ResEquCoV)
    }
      
    if (tail(Spher[["Mauchly's Test for Sphericity"]][["p"]][2], n = 1) <= 0.05) {
      ResSpher <- "Sphericity violated"
      print(ResSpher)
    } else {
      ResSpher <- "Sphericity holds"
      print(ResSpher)
    }
      
      
  # HYPOTHESIS TESTING SELECTION #############################################
  
  for (xx in 1:100) {
    
    # Make decision about data transformation   
    cc <- readline("Select statistical test to run based on assumption tests:
                    0 = Exist loop
                    1 = Standard two-way mixed ANOVA
                    2 = Robust two-way mixed ANOVA
                    3 = Aligned Rank Transform for Nonparametric Factorial ANOVA")
    
    if (cc == 0) { # Leave the loop
      
      break
    
    } else if (cc == 1) { # Standard two-way mixed ANOVA if assumptions are met
      
      # 1. Two-way Mixed ANOVA (standard)
      res.aov <- rstatix::anova_test( # This version is suitable if there are no ouliers
          data = BldCnt, dv = Counts, wid = Guinea_Pig,
          between = State, within = Treatment
          ) # Greenhouse-Geisser sphericity correction automatically applied if Mauchly's test is significant (p<0.05)
      
      ResAovT <- "Standard two-way Mixed ANOVA"
      print(ResAovT)
      
      
      # Post-Hoc analysis for significant interaction
      if (tail(res.aov[["ANOVA"]][["p"]][3], n = 1) <= 0.05) { 
      
        # A 1.1 One-way ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
        res.aovBetween <- BldCnt %>%
          group_by(Treatment) %>%
          rstatix::anova_test( # This version is suitable if there are no outliers
           data = ., dv = Counts, wid = Guinea_Pig,
           between = State
            ) %>%
          get_anova_table() %>%
          adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
        
        ResAovTBetween <- "One-way ANOVA"
        print(ResAovTBetween)
        
          # A 1.1.1 Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
          PairCompBetween <- BldCnt %>%
            group_by(Treatment) %>%
            pairwise_t_test(Counts ~ State, 
                            paired = FALSE, 
                            p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTBetween = "Pairwise t test"
        
        # A 1.2. One-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the within-subject factor)
        res.aovWithin <- BldCnt %>%
          group_by(State) %>%
          rstatix::anova_test( # This version is suitable if there are no outliers
           data = ., dv = Counts, wid = Guinea_Pig,
           within = Treatment
            ) %>%
          get_anova_table() %>%
          adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
        
        ResAovTWithin <- "One-way Repeated Measures ANOVA"
        print(ResAovTWithin)
        
          # A 1.2.1 Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
          PairCompWithin <- BldCnt %>%
            group_by(State) %>%
            pairwise_t_test(Counts ~ Treatment, 
                            paired = TRUE, 
                            p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTWithin = "Pairwise Paired t tests"
        
        
      } else { # Post-Hoc analysis for non-significant interaction
        
        # B 1.1. One-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
        res.aovBetween <- NA
        
          ResAovTBetween <- "No significant interaction"
          print(ResAovTBetween)
        
          # B 1.1.1. Pairwise comparison (for between-subject factor)
          PairCompBetween <- BldCnt %>%
            pairwise_t_test(Counts ~ State, 
                            paired = FALSE, 
                            p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTBetween <- "Pairwise t test"
        
        # B 1.2. One-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the within-subject factor)
        res.aovWithin <- NA
          
          ResAovTWithin <- "No significant interaction"
          print(ResAovTWithin)
        
          # B 1.2.1. Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
          PairCompWithin <- BldCnt %>%
            pairwise_t_test(Counts ~ Treatment, 
                            paired = TRUE, 
                            p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTWithin <- "Pairwise Paired t tests"
      }
    
      
  } else if (cc == 2) { # Robust analysis if assumptions are not met
    
    # Robust Two-way Mixed ANOVA
    res.aov <- bwtrim(Counts ~ State * Treatment, 
                      id = Guinea_Pig, 
                      tr = 0.1,
                      data = BldCnt)
    
      ResAovT <- "Robust two-way Mixed ANOVA"
      print(ResAovT)
    
      # Assessing each variable and their interaction separately
      SinEff1 <- sppba(Counts ~ State * Treatment, 
                       id = Guinea_Pig,
                       tr = 0.1,
                       data = BldCnt) # between groups effect only (MOM estimator)
      
      SinEff2 <- sppbb(Counts ~ State * Treatment, 
                       id = Guinea_Pig,
                       tr = 0.1,
                       data = BldCnt) # within groups effect only (MOM estimator)
      
      SinEff3 <- sppbi(Counts ~ State * Treatment, 
                       id = Guinea_Pig,
                       tr = 0.1,
                       data = BldCnt) # interaction effect only (MOM estimator)
      
    
    if (res.aov$AB.p.value <= 0.05) { # Post-Hoc analysis for significant interaction
      
      # Robust one-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the within-subject factor) 
      res.aovWithin <- lapply(levels(BldCnt$State), function(x) { # Executes the one-way RM ANOVA for each group separately
        with(subset(BldCnt, subset = State == x),
          rmanova(y = Counts,
                  groups = Treatment, 
                  block = Guinea_Pig,
                  tr = 0.1))
        }) %>%
        setNames(levels(BldCnt$State)) %>%
        lapply(., function(y) {
          bind_cols(y[!names(y) %in% "call"])
        }) %>%
        bind_rows(.) %>%
        adjust_pvalue(method = "BH") %>%
        add_column(State = levels(BldCnt$State),
                   Effect = rep("Treatment", 
                                times = length(levels(BldCnt$State))),
                   .before = "test")
      
      ResAovTWithin <- "Robust one-way repeated ANOVA"
      print(ResAovTWithin)
      
      
      if (length(levels(BldCnt$Treatment)) > 2) { # Execute if within-subject factor has more than 2 levels; for 2 levels rmanova() is equivalent to pairwise comparison
        
        # Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
        PairCompWithin <- lapply(levels(BldCnt$State), function(x) { # Executes the pariwise test for each group separately
          with(subset(BldCnt, subset = State == x),
               rmmcp(y = Counts, 
                     groups = Treatment, 
                     block = Guinea_Pig,
                     tr = 0.1))
          }) %>%
          setNames(levels(BldCnt$State)) %>%
          lapply(., function(y) {
            as.data.frame(y$comp) %>%
              set_colnames(make.unique(colnames(.))) %>%
          mutate(across(grep("Group", colnames(.)), ~ifelse(. == 1, "Pre-Treatment", 
                                                            ifelse(. == 2, "Pre-Infestation", "Post-Infestation"))))
          }) %>%
          bind_rows(., .id = "Level")
        
        ResPCTWithin <- "Robust pairwise paired comparison"
        print(ResPCTWithin)
      
        
      } else {
        
        PairCompWithin <- NA
        
        ResPCTWithin <- "Robust pairwise paired comparison not executed"
        print(ResPCTWithin)
      }
    
      # Robust one-way ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
      res.aovBetween <- lapply(levels(BldCnt$Treatment), function(x) {
        t1way(formula = Counts ~ State, 
              data = subset(BldCnt, subset = Treatment == x), 
              tr = 0.1) %>%
          append(., split(.$effsize_ci, 
                          f = c("effsize_ci_lower", "effsize_ci_upper")), 
                 after = 5) %>%
          .[!names(.) %in% c("effsize_ci", "alpha", "call")]
        }) %>%
        setNames(levels(BldCnt$Treatment)) %>%
        lapply(., function(y) {
          bind_cols(y[!names(y) %in% "call"])
        }) %>%
        bind_rows(., .id = "Treatment") %>%
        adjust_pvalue(method = "BH") %>%
        add_column(Effect = rep("State", 
                                times = length(levels(BldCnt$Treatment))),
                   .before = "test")
      
      
      ResAovTBetween <- "Robust one-way ANOVA"
      print(ResAovTBetween)
      
      
      # Execute if within-subject factor has more than 2 levels
      if (length(levels(BldCnt$State)) > 2) { 
         
        # Pairwise comparison (for between-subject factor)
        PairCompBetween <- lapply(levels(BldCnt$Treatment), function(x) {
          lincon(formula = Counts ~ State, 
                 data = subset(BldCnt, subset = Treatment == x), 
                 tr = 0.1, 
                 method = "BH")
          }) %>%
          setNames(levels(BldCnt$Treatment)) %>%
          lapply(., function(y) {
            as.data.frame(y$comp) %>%
              set_colnames(make.unique(colnames(.))) %>%
              mutate(across(grep("Group", colnames(.)), 
                            ~ifelse(. == 1, "FTY720", 
                                    ifelse(. == 2, "Naive", "PBS")))) 
          }) %>%
          bind_rows(., .id = "Level") %>%
          adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
         
        ResPCTBetween <- "Robust pairwise comparison"
        print(ResPCTBetween)
        
        
        } else { # for 2 levels t1way() is equivalent to pairwise comparison
          
          PairCompBetween <- NA
      
          ResPCTBetween <- "Robust pairwise comparison not executed"
          print(ResPCTBetween)
        
        }
      
      
    } else { # Post-Hoc analysis for non-significant interaction
      
      # Robust one-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the within-subject factor)
      res.aovWithin <- NA
      
      ResAovTWithin <- "No significant interaction"
      print(ResAovTWithin)
      
      
      # Execute if within-subject factor has more than 2 level
      if (length(levels(BldCnt$Treatment)) > 2) { 
        
        # Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
        PairCompWithin <- with(BldCnt,
               rmmcp(y = Counts, 
                     groups = Treatment, 
                     block = Guinea_Pig,
                     tr = 0.1)) %>%
          .$comp %>%
          as.data.frame(.) %>%
          set_colnames(make.unique(colnames(.))) %>%
          mutate(across(grep("Group", colnames(.)), ~ifelse(. == 1, "Pre-Treatment",
                                                            ifelse(. == 2, "Pre-Infestation", "Post-Infestation")))) %>%
          adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
        
        ResPCTWithin <- "Robust pairwise paired comparison (rmmcp)"
        print(ResPCTWithin)
        
        
      } else {
        
        # Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
        PairCompWithin <- with(BldCnt,
          rmanova(y = Counts,
                  groups = Treatment, 
                  block = Guinea_Pig,
                  tr = 0.1)) %>%
          .[c(1:4)] %>%
          bind_cols(.) %>%
          as.data.frame %>%
          set_rownames("Treatment")
        
        ResPCTWithin <- "Robust pairwise paired comparison (rmanova)"
        print(ResPCTWithin)
      }
    
      
      # Robust one-way ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
      res.aovBetween <- NA
      
      ResAovTBetween <- "No significant interaction"
      print(ResAovTBetween)
      
      
      if (length(levels(BldCnt$State)) > 2) { # Execute if within-subject factor has more than 2 levels; for 2 levels rmanova() is equivalent to pairwise comparison
         
        # Pairwise comparison (for between-subject factor)
        PairCompBetween <- lincon(formula = Counts ~ State, 
                 data = BldCnt, 
                 tr = 0.1, 
                 method = "BH") %>%
          .$comp %>%
          as.data.frame(.) %>%
          set_colnames(make.unique(colnames(.))) %>%
          mutate(across(grep("Group", colnames(.)),
                        ~ifelse(. == 1, "FTY720", 
                                ifelse(. == 2, "Naive", "PBS")))) %>%
          adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
         
        ResPCTBetween <- "Robust pairwise comparison"
        print(ResPCTBetween)
        
        
        } else {
          
          # Robust one-way ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
          PairCompBetween <- t1way(formula = Counts ~ State,
                                    data = BldCnt,
                                    tr = 0.1) %>%
              append(., split(.$effsize_ci, 
                              f = c("effsize_ci_lower", "effsize_ci_upper")), 
                     after = 5) %>%
              .[!names(.) %in% c("effsize_ci", "alpha", "call")] %>%
            bind_cols(.) %>%
            as.data.frame(.) %>%
            set_rownames("State")
          
      
          ResPCTBetween <- "Robust pairwise paired comparison not executed"
          print(ResPCTBetween)
        }
      }
      
      # Summarize robust two-way mixed ANOVA into a printable dataframe                
      res.aov <- as.data.frame(rbind(c(unlist(res.aov[c(1,3,2)])),
                                        c(unlist(res.aov[c(4,6,5)])),
                                        c(unlist(res.aov[c(7,9,8)]))) %>%
                                    set_rownames(c(res.aov$call$formula[[3]][[2]],
                                                   res.aov$call$formula[[3]][[3]],
                                                   paste(res.aov$call$formula[[3]][[2]],
                                                         res.aov$call$formula[[3]][[3]],
                                                         sep = ":"))) %>% 
                                    set_colnames(c("value", "df1", "df2", "p.value"))) %>%
        mutate(., "sig." = .[["p.value"]] %>%
                 symnum(.,
                        cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
                        symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", "ns"))) %>%
        mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", round(.x, 4)))) %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column(., var = "Factor")
        
      
  } else if (cc == 3) { # non-parametric alternative for two-way mixed ANOVA
    
    # Aligned Rank Transform for Nonparametric Factorial ANOVA
    
    # Check if transformation is valid (all output = 0)
    tryCatch({summary(ARTool::art(Counts ~ Treatment * State + Error(Guinea_Pig), 
                                  data = BldCnt)); EM <<- 0}, 
             # If not all output = 0 a warning is thrown
             warning = function(w) {EM <<- 1})
             
    # Select test
    if (EM == 0) {
      
      # Aligned Rank Transform for Nonparametric Factorial ANOVA
      res.aov <- anova(ARTool::art(Counts ~ Treatment * State + Error(Guinea_Pig),
                                   data = BldCnt))
      
      ResAovT <- "Aligned Rank Transform for Nonparametric Factorial ANOVA"
      print(ResAovT)
      
      # Post-Hoc analysis for significant interaction
      if (tail(res.aov[, "Pr(>F)"], n = 1) <= 0.05) { 
      
        # A 1.1 Kruskal-Wallis test (effect of the between-subject factor)
        res.aovBetween <- list(
          "Kruskal-Wallis test" = BldCnt %>%
            group_by(Treatment) %>%
            rstatix::kruskal_test(Counts ~ State, 
             data = .) %>%
            adjust_pvalue(method = "BH"),
          
          "Kruskal-Wallis effect size" = BldCnt %>%
            group_by(Treatment) %>%
            rstatix::kruskal_effsize(Counts ~ State, 
             data = .))
        
        ResAovTBetween <- "Kruskal-Wallis test"
        print(ResAovTBetween)
        
          # A 1.1.1 Pairwise comparison by Dunn's test (for between-subject factor)
          PairCompBetween <- BldCnt %>%
            group_by(Treatment) %>%
            dunn_test(Counts ~ State,
                      p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTBetween = "Dunn's test"
          print(ResPCTBetween)
        
        # A 1.2. Friedman test (effect of the within-subject factor)
        res.aovWithin <- list(
          "Friedman test" = BldCnt %>%
            group_by(State) %>%
            rstatix::friedman_test(Counts ~ Treatment | Guinea_Pig,
                                   data = .) %>%
            adjust_pvalue(method = "BH"),
        
          "Friedman effect size" = BldCnt %>%
            group_by(State) %>%
            rstatix::friedman_effsize(Counts ~ Treatment | Guinea_Pig,
                                 data = .))
        
        ResAovTWithin <- "Friedman test"
        print(ResAovTWithin)
        
          # A 1.2.1 Pairwise comparison by exact all-pairs comparisons tests (for within-subject factor)
          PairCompWithin <- lapply(levels(BldCnt$State), function (aa) {
            
            xxx <- BldCnt[BldCnt$State %in% aa,] %>%
              dplyr::select(!State) %>%
              pivot_wider(., names_from = Treatment, values_from = Counts) %>%
              tibble::column_to_rownames("Guinea_Pig") %>%
              as.matrix(.)
              
              # Post-hoc exact all-pairs comparisons test
              PairComp <- PMCMRplus::frdAllPairsExactTest(y = as.matrix(xxx), p.adjust.method = "BH")
              
              PMCMRTable(PairComp) %>%
                mutate(., across("p.value", as.numeric)) %>%
                mutate(., "sig." = .[["p.value"]] %>%
                         symnum(.,
                                cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
                                symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", "ns"))) %>%
                mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", round(.x, 4))))
            
            }) %>%
            setNames(levels(BldCnt$State)) %>%
            bind_rows(., .id = "State")
            
          ResPCTWithin = "Exact all-pairs comparisons tests"
          print(ResPCTWithin)
        
        
      } else { # Post-Hoc analysis for non-significant interaction
        
        # B 1.1. One-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the between-subject factor)
        res.aovBetween <- NA
        
          ResAovTBetween <- "No significant interaction"
          print(ResAovTBetween)
        
          # B 1.1.1. Pairwise comparison (for between-subject factor)
          PairCompBetween <- BldCnt %>%
            dunn_test(Counts ~ State,
                      p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
          ResPCTBetween = "Dunn's test"
          print(ResPCTBetween)
        
        # B 1.2. One-way repeated measures ANOVA (effect of the within-subject factor)
        res.aovWithin <- NA
          
          ResAovTWithin <- "No significant interaction"
          print(ResAovTWithin)
        
          # B 1.2.1. Pairwise comparison (for within-subject factor)
          PairCompWithin <- lapply(list(BldCnt), function (aa) {
            
            xxx <- aa %>%
              dplyr::select(!State) %>%
              pivot_wider(., names_from = Treatment, values_from = Counts) %>%
              tibble::column_to_rownames("Guinea_Pig") %>%
              as.matrix(.)
          
              # Post-hoc exact all-pairs comparisons test
              PairComp <- PMCMRplus::frdAllPairsExactTest(y = as.matrix(xxx), p.adjust.method = "BH")
          
              # Convert output to table format
              PMCMRTable(PairComp) %>%
                mutate(., across("p.value", as.numeric)) %>%
                mutate(., "sig." = .[["p.value"]] %>%
                         symnum(.,
                                cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
                                symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", "ns"))) %>%
                mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", round(.x, 4))))
            
            })
            
          ResPCTWithin = "Exact all-pairs comparisons tests"
          print(ResPCTWithin)
      }
    
    } else {
      
      print("ART transformation may not be applicable")
      
    }
  }
  }
      
  # COLLATE DATA----------------------------------------------------------------
    
  # Collate the test outcome calls
  AssTest <- as.data.frame(rbind("Dat_Transformation"                         = ResTrans,
                                 "Transformation for skewness and kurtosis"   = ResTransSK,
                                 "Data_Normality_Assumption"                  = ResNormUV,
                                 "Residual_Normality_Assumption"              = ResNormRes,
                                 "Outliers"                                   = ResOutUV,
                                 "Homogeneity_of_Variance"                    = ResEquVar,
                                 "Homogeneity_of_Covariance"                  = ResEquCoV,
                                 "Maulchy's test for sphericity"              = ResSpher,
                                 "2-way_Mixed_ANOVA_Test_applied"             = ResAovT,
                                 "1-way_Repeated_Measures_ANOVA_Test_applied" = ResAovTWithin,
                                 "Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Within)"    = ResPCTWithin,
                                 "1-way_ANOVA_Test_applied"                   = ResAovTBetween,
                                 "Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Between)"   = ResPCTBetween
                                 )) %>%
    setNames(., "Outcome")
  
  # Compile output data list
  AovDat <- list("Summary"                                  = SumStat,
                 "Data Box plot"                            = DatDis,
                 "Assumption_Test_Outcome"                  = AssTest,
                 "Data_Normality_Assumption"                = NormUV,
                 "QQ plot: by groups"                       = qqplotBld,
                 "Skewness and Kurtsosis"                   = SkeKur,
                 "Residual_Normality_Assumption"            = NormRes,
                 "QQ plotof residuals"                      = qqplotRes,
                 "Outliers"                                 = OutLierUV,
                 "Box plot"                                 = BoxPlotUV,
                 "Homogeneity_of_Variance"                  = EquVar,
                 "Homogeneity_of_Covariance"                = BoxM,
                 "Residuals_vs_Fitted"                      = EquVarPlot,
                 "Maulchy's_test_of_sphericity"             = Spher,
                 "2-way_Mixed_ANOVA"                        = res.aov,
                 "1-way_Repeated_Measures_ANOVA_Type"       = res.aovWithin,
                 "Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Within)"  = PairCompWithin,
                 "1-way_ANOVA_Type"                         = res.aovBetween,
                 "Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Between)" = PairCompBetween
                 )
  }) %>%
    setNames("LYMPH")
})
```

```{r create-output-table, include = FALSE}
## Collat the data we want to export
DatOut <- lapply(ResBld, function(xx) {
  lapply(xx, function(yy) {
  
    list(yy[["2-way_Mixed_ANOVA"]],
         yy[["1-way_Repeated_Measures_ANOVA_Type"]],
         yy[["Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Within)"]],
         yy[["1-way_ANOVA_Type"]],
         yy[["Pairwise_Post_Hoc_Test_applied_(Between)"]])
  }) %>%
    unlist(., recursive = FALSE) %>%
    purrr::set_names(c("Two way Mixed ANOVA", 
                       "One-way Repeated Measures ANOVA",
                       "Pairwise Comparison by within factor",
                       "One-way ANOVA",
                       "Pairwise Comparison by between factor"))
}) %>%
  # unlist(., recursive = FALSE) %>%
  purrr::set_names(names(ResBld))

# Produce tables of the pairwise Cox PH models
mapply(function(aa, bb) {
  
  mapply(function(xx, yy) {
    
    if (!hasName(yy, "sig.")) { 
      # Get the data adjusted
      if (length(yy) != 1) {
        Dat <- yy %>%
          mutate("sig." = symnum(
              if (ncol(pick(matches("adj\\.p"))) > 0) {
                pick(matches("adj\\.p"))[[1]] # Select the first matched column
              } else {
                p.value # Fallback to the standard p.value column
              },
              cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 1),
              symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "+", " "),
              abbr.colnames = FALSE,
              na = ""
            )) %>%
            mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))) %>%
            mutate(., across(contains("p.value"), ~ ifelse(.x < 0.0001, "<0.0001", .x)))
          
        } else {
          
          Dat <- as.data.frame("NA")
        }
    } else {
      Dat <- yy %>%
        mutate(., across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
      
    }
    
    if (ncol(Dat) > 1) {
      
      # Turn it into a table
      gtsave(data =
             Dat %>%
               as.data.frame() %>%
               # Build a table
               gt() %>%
               tab_header(
                 title = xx,
                 subtitle = bb
                 ) %>%
               tab_style(
                 style = cell_text(align = "center"),
                 locations = cells_column_labels()),
             filename = paste0(bb, xx, ".png"),
             path = paste(here(), "Output", "Tables", "LYMPH", bb, sep = "/"))
    } else {
      
    }
  }, xx = names(aa),
     yy = aa)
  
}, aa = DatOut,
   bb = names(DatOut))
```
